title: Athlete's heart: eccentric hypertrophy raises stroke volume (pulmonic flow murmur)
vignette: A 28-year-old professional endurance athlete comes to the office after his team physician detected a heart murmur. The patient has no symptoms and has no exercise limitations. Medical history is nonsignificant. Blood pressure is 110/66 mm Hg and pulse is 54/min. Physical examination shows a soft systolic murmur best heard at the left second intercostal space in the supine position. The murmur disappears when the patient is upright but reappears after brief exercise. Which of the following cardiovascular adaptations best explains this patient's finding?

clues.note: Endurance (isotonic) training produces ECCENTRIC hypertrophy - chamber enlargement that increases diastolic filling and stroke volume ('athlete's heart').
Resting bradycardia (high vagal tone + high stroke volume) is a normal athletic adaptation; cardiac output is maintained by the increased stroke volume.

clues.text: soft systolic murmur best heard at the left second intercostal space
clues.note: The left 2nd intercostal space is the pulmonic area; a soft systolic murmur here reflects high-velocity flow across the pulmonic valve - a benign flow murmur.

clues.text: murmur disappears when the patient is upright but reappears after brief exercise
clues.note: Standing reduces venous return (less flow -> murmur softens); exercise increases venous return/stroke volume (more flow -> murmur returns) - hallmark of a FLOW murmur, not structural disease.

whatMatters: Endurance training causes ECCENTRIC hypertrophy (LV and RV cavity enlargement) that increases DIASTOLIC FILLING and STROKE VOLUME. The high stroke volume drives a benign pulmonic FLOW murmur that varies with venous return (gone when upright, back after exercise). Answer C.
strategy: Recognize benign athlete's heart: resting bradycardia + a flow murmur that changes with preload. The underlying adaptation is INCREASED STROKE VOLUME from eccentric (volume-load) hypertrophy. Reject increased wall thickness (that's concentric hypertrophy from resistance/pressure training and wouldn't create a preload-dependent flow murmur), decreased vagal tone (athletes have INCREASED vagal tone -> bradycardia), decreased pulmonary capacitance and increased SVR (endurance training INCREASES capacitance and DECREASES SVR).

eliminations.label: Decreased pulmonary capacitance - opposite in athletes
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: reduced ability of the pulmonary vasculature to accommodate volume. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: endurance training INCREASES pulmonary vascular capacitance to handle high flow; decreased capacitance doesn't explain a benign flow murmur. ✅ Correct if: pulmonary vascular disease reducing compliance.

eliminations.label: Decreased vagal tone - athletes have increased tone
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: less parasympathetic input to the heart. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the athlete's resting bradycardia reflects INCREASED vagal tone, not decreased; decreased tone would raise heart rate. ✅ Correct if: explaining resting tachycardia.

eliminations.label: Increased SVR - endurance lowers SVR
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: higher systemic vascular resistance. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: endurance training lowers resting SVR (skeletal muscle vasodilation, capillary density); high SVR is a resistance-training/pressure-load feature. ✅ Correct if: chronic pressure overload (hypertension).

eliminations.label: Increased wall thickness - concentric (resistance) hypertrophy
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: thickened ventricular walls (concentric hypertrophy). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that is the response to resistance/pressure training and would not generate a benign, preload-dependent pulmonic flow murmur; endurance training causes ECCENTRIC (cavity-enlarging) change with increased stroke volume. ✅ Correct if: heavy weightlifting/pressure overload with concentric LVH.

reasoning: Endurance training -> eccentric hypertrophy (LV/RV cavity enlargement)
Larger chambers increase diastolic filling and stroke volume
High stroke volume produces a benign pulmonic flow murmur that varies with venous return
mechanism: 'ATHLETE'S HEART' reflects physiologic remodeling that differs by training type. Intense ENDURANCE (isotonic) training increases blood volume and left ventricular VOLUME load, producing ECCENTRIC hypertrophy (LV wall lengthening with increased cavity size); the right ventricle enlarges as well. Larger chambers increase diastolic filling capacity and thus STROKE VOLUME and cardiac output, while resting heart rate falls (elevated vagal tone) - stroke volume compensates to keep cardiac output normal at rest. The high stroke volume drives high-velocity flow across the slightly smaller pulmonic valve, producing a benign PULMONIC FLOW MURMUR best heard at the left second intercostal space in the supine position; it softens on standing (reduced venous return) and returns after exercise (increased venous return). By contrast, RESISTANCE (isometric) training causes pressure-load CONCENTRIC hypertrophy (increased wall thickness with a normal cavity), which would not produce this preload-dependent flow murmur. Endurance training also decreases resting SVR and increases pulmonary vascular capacitance.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid CV/physiology > athlete's heart: endurance -> eccentric hypertrophy (increased cavity, stroke volume, high vagal tone/bradycardia); resistance -> concentric hypertrophy (wall thickening); benign flow murmurs vary with preload.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Endurance training enlarges chambers -> higher stroke volume -> benign pulmonic flow murmur.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on eccentric vs concentric hypertrophy, stroke volume, vagal tone, pulmonic flow murmur, or venous return? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Wall thickening = concentric (resistance) training; athletes have INCREASED vagal tone, INCREASED pulmonary capacitance, DECREASED SVR.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: endurance -> eccentric hypertrophy -> increased stroke volume (flow murmur); resistance -> concentric hypertrophy (thick walls).

keywords.back: Eccentric hypertrophy -> increased cavity size and stroke volume
Increased vagal tone + high stroke volume
Softer standing (less preload), louder after exercise (more preload)

keywords.front: Endurance effect on SVR / pulmonary capacitance

firstAid.detail: CV: eccentric hypertrophy -> increased stroke volume; benign pulmonic flow murmur.
CV > flow murmurs vary with venous return (standing vs exercise).

memoryHook: Endurance stretches the heart into a bigger balloon (eccentric) - each beat ejects more blood, and that extra flow whistles across the pulmonic valve only when the tank is full.
